name: Platform-to-Business (P2B) Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: Commission compliance review and national regulator surveys/sweeps only; no study of effects on business users' sales, prices or competition
summary: The P2B Regulation (applying since July 2020) gave businesses that sell through platforms rights to clear terms, ranking explanations and complaint handling. The Commission forecast EUR 0.8-4 billion of extra online trade but never measured it; its 2023 review and later national checks found low compliance (around 80% of platforms in an Irish 2025 sweep) and low awareness among businesses. In November 2025 the Commission proposed repealing it as largely overtaken by the DSA and DMA.

indicators.objective: The proposal has no LFS indicator section; its memorandum promised monitoring through the EU Observatory on the Online Platform Economy (number and types of business users, complaints handled, cases solved, time to resolve) and a review three years after entry into force

indicators.indicator: Number and type of complaints handled through internal complaint-handling, cases solved, time to resolve
indicators.evidence: Only 19 of 179 platforms studied published the mandatory complaint-handling report; reported numbers range from 12 complaints (Apple) to over 3 million (Google), showing divergent interpretations and possible non-compliance.
Only 25 of 179 large and medium platforms named the required two mediators; no specialised mediation bodies set up; very few complaints or court cases.

indicators.indicator: Disclosure of main ranking parameters and of differentiated treatment
indicators.evidence: Only about a third of platforms reviewed listed ranking parameters in their terms; 10% of business users report little or no ranking information and 42% only moderate. Irish CCPC sweep (late 2025): about 80% of 17 platforms non-compliant in some respect.

indicators.indicator: Business users aware of and using their new rights
indicators.evidence: Low: Irish survey (2022, n=177) found 51% of businesses had no knowledge of the Regulation and 4% detailed knowledge; Commission 2023 review reports a lack of awareness, lower where Member States set up no public enforcement.

indicators.indicator: Reversing a trust-related 'dampening effect' on the online platform economy worth EUR 0.81-4.05bn
indicators.evidence: Not measured. The 2023 review assessed compliance only; in November 2025 the Commission proposed repealing the Regulation as having 'only residual value' after the DSA and DMA.

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Impact assessment accompanying the proposal on fairness and transparency for business users of online intermediation services (executive summary SWD(2018) 139), SWD(2018) 138
literature.title: Impact assessment accompanying the proposal on fairness and transparency for business users of online intermediation services (executive summary SWD(2018) 139)
literature.headline: Preferred option would reverse a trust-related dampening effect on the platform economy worth EUR 0.81-4.05bn; costs up to about 1 FTE for small platforms and about 0.03% of turnover for large ones; no costs for merchants
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected fairer, more transparent platform terms to unlock EUR 0.8-4 billion of extra online trade at small cost to platforms.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), First preliminary review on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 (with SWD(2023) 300), COM(2023) 525
literature.title: First preliminary review on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 (with SWD(2023) 300)
literature.method: review (support study: 308 interviews, survey of business users in 8 Member States, review of terms of 300 platforms, focus groups)
literature.headline: Initial positive effects but full potential not reached; widespread non-compliance and low awareness; only about a third of platforms disclose ranking parameters; 19 of 179 publish complaint reports; 25 of 179 list two mediators
literature.summary_plain: Three years in, the Commission found that most platforms were not fully complying and most businesses did not know their rights.

literature.citation: Sovrano, Lognoul & Bacchelli (2024), An Empirical Study on Compliance with Ranking Transparency in the Software Documentation of EU Online Platforms, ICSE-SEIS 2024 (arXiv 2312.14794)
literature.title: An Empirical Study on Compliance with Ranking Transparency in the Software Documentation of EU Online Platforms
literature.method: descriptive compliance audit (six platforms) plus automated assessment tools
literature.headline: Substantial differences in how Amazon, Bing, Booking, Google, Tripadvisor and Yahoo document ranking under P2B Article 5; compliance remains a challenge
literature.summary_plain: An audit of six major platforms found very uneven explanations of how they rank sellers and results, as the Regulation requires.

literature.citation: Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (Ireland) / Ipsos (2023), Platform to Business research: survey of businesses using online platforms (Q4 2022), CCPC
literature.authors: Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (Ireland) / Ipsos
literature.title: Platform to Business research: survey of businesses using online platforms (Q4 2022)
literature.headline: 51% of businesses had no knowledge of the P2B Regulation, 21% knew only its name, 24% its main provisions, 4% detailed knowledge
literature.summary_plain: Half of Irish businesses selling through platforms had never heard of the rules meant to protect them.

literature.citation: Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (Ireland) (2026), CCPC conducts sweep of online platforms to identify potential breaches of the Platform to Business Regulation, CCPC press release, 1 May 2026
literature.title: CCPC conducts sweep of online platforms to identify potential breaches of the Platform to Business Regulation
literature.headline: About 80% of platforms swept had some element of non-compliance (complaint handling, mediation, terms); followed a notable rise in complaints in 2025
literature.summary_plain: Six years after the rules took effect, Ireland's regulator found about four in five platforms checked still breached them in some way.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Proposal for a Digital Omnibus Regulation (repealing, among others, Regulation (EU) 2019/1150), COM(2025) 837
literature.title: Proposal for a Digital Omnibus Regulation (repealing, among others, Regulation (EU) 2019/1150)
literature.headline: Proposes repeal of the P2B Regulation: DSA and DMA have largely overtaken it, it has 'only residual value'; cites 2023 review finding low awareness, insufficient compliance and very limited complaints
literature.summary_plain: In November 2025 the Commission proposed scrapping the P2B Regulation, saying newer platform laws had overtaken it.
